overview: Goyocephale was a small pachycephalosaurian ornithischian from Late Cretaceous Mongolia. Unlike many dome-headed dinosaurs known mainly from skull roofs, it is represented by a disarticulated skeleton including much of the skull, limbs, pelvis and vertebrae, giving a broader view of pachycephalosaur anatomy.

Its name means "decorated head", combining Mongolian and Greek roots, and the species name honours Owen Lattimore. PBDB records it from Omnogov, Mongolia, but formation-level data still needs manual confirmation in this dataset.

articles.title: Why it matters
articles.body: Goyocephale gives useful postcranial information for pachycephalosaurs, a group often represented by skull domes rather than fuller skeletons.

articles.title: Evidence limit
articles.body: The local PBDB record lacks formation detail, so ecological comparisons should stay regional until the source locality is manually verified.

record.description: Goyocephale lattimorei was a flat-headed pachycephalosaurid from the Baruungoyot Formation of Mongolia. One partial skull and associated incomplete skeleton preserve much of the jaw, skull roof, vertebral column and limbs, but the specimen is not complete.
facts: The flat skull roof is a genuine feature, though maturity influences pachycephalosaur skull shape.
Large canine-like teeth do not by themselves prove carnivory.
Bipedal locomotion is well supported; detailed diet and head-use behaviour are not.

review.ageReviewNote: The Baruungoyot Formation is Campanian; its local numerical calibration is approximate.
